nodes.name: Local.ComputeForBestProds
nodes.summary: A DAX user-defined function that evaluates an expression only for products appearing in the top-N across a coverage fraction of visible years. Uses GENERATE, TOPN, GROUPBY, and SUMX(CURRENTGROUP(), 1) to count year appearances and filter to evergreen top-N products.

nodes.name: Local.* UDF Wrapper Pattern
nodes.summary: Use the Local. prefix for model-dependent wrapper functions that call model-independent library functions. This separates model-specific column mapping from reusable business logic, enabling multiple models to share the same library function without conflicts.

nodes.name: Measure Library to UDF Library Migration
nodes.summary: Systematic 6-step approach for refactoring copy-pasted measures into a typed UDF library. Includes audit, parameter categorization, default values, XML documentation, version control in TMDL, and deployment via XMLA or semantic link.

nodes.name: Model-Dependent vs Model-Independent UDFs
nodes.summary: The fundamental distinction in DAX UDF design: model-dependent functions contain hard-coded table/column references specific to one semantic model; model-independent functions receive all model objects as parameters and work across any model.

nodes.name: PREVIOUS-based YoY% Visual Calculation Pattern
nodes.summary: A visual calculation pattern for Year-over-Year percentage change using PREVIOUS() on the COLUMNS axis. Faster than SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR for small virtual tables with DISTINCTCOUNT, but slower for large matrices due to densification overhead.

nodes.name: Performance Analyzer vs DAX Studio
nodes.summary: Power BI Performance Analyzer measures which visual is slow and how long each component takes, but cannot diagnose why. DAX Studio exposes SE/FE timings and query plans to explain why. Use Performance Analyzer first, then DAX Studio for diagnosis.

nodes.name: REMOVEFILTERS vs ALLSELECTED for Per-Level Rules
nodes.summary: Inside per-level conditional formatting measures, REMOVEFILTERS compares against full model totals ignoring slicers, while ALLSELECTED respects the visual's visible date range. The choice determines whether shading is relative to all-time or currently-displayed totals.

nodes.name: SE/FE Performance Model: The Warehouse Analogy
nodes.summary: Storage Engine (SE) and Formula Engine (FE) have contrasting performance characteristics: SE scans in parallel like warehouse workers counting pages; FE compares sequentially like a manager reading 1000 result slips. FE-heavy queries and FE repeatedly re-triggering SE are danger signals.

nodes.name: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS Blank Elimination + VC Densification Interaction
nodes.summary: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS eliminates blank rows as an optimization while visual calculation densification recreates those rows so PREVIOUS/NEXT can navigate the full cross-product. This conflict is the root cause of VC performance degradation on large sparse virtual tables.

nodes.name: SWITCH-Level-Dispatch Pattern
nodes.summary: Apply different DAX logic depending on which level of a hierarchy a cell belongs to using SWITCH TRUE with ISINSCOPE or ISATLEVEL. Each branch is independent with its own CALCULATE or COLLAPSE logic for per-level arithmetic.

nodes.name: SWITCH Specificity-Ordering Pattern
nodes.summary: When dispatching on hierarchy level using ISINSCOPE or ISATLEVEL, test from most specific to least specific column. Because ISINSCOPE returns TRUE for all ancestor levels simultaneously, most-specific-first ordering ensures the correct branch fires at each cell.

nodes.name: DAX UDF Library Function
nodes.summary: A reusable DAX function defined with DEFINE FUNCTION that encapsulates business logic. Model-independent library functions use parameters for all model objects, enabling cross-model portability.

nodes.name: Local.* Wrapper Function
nodes.summary: A model-dependent DAX function prefixed with Local. that maps model-specific columns to model-independent library function parameters.

nodes.name: Storage Engine (SE)
nodes.summary: The DAX engine component that performs parallel column scans and aggregations in the data cache, typically handling the heavy lifting of query execution.

nodes.name: Formula Engine (FE)
nodes.summary: The DAX engine component that performs sequential operations on storage engine results, including complex calculations and cross-joins.

nodes.name: Visual Calculations (VC)
nodes.summary: Power BI feature that computes values within the visual layer using PREVIOUS, COLLAPSE, RUNNINGSUM and similar functions operating on the virtual table structure.

nodes.name: ISINSCOPE
nodes.summary: DAX function that returns TRUE when a column is in the filter context at a specific level of a hierarchy, enabling level-aware measure logic.

nodes.name: ISATLEVEL
nodes.summary: Visual calculation function that detects which level of the visual hierarchy the current cell belongs to, used in COLLAPSE/COLLAPSEALL navigation.

nodes.name: TOPN
nodes.summary: DAX function that returns the top N rows of a table ordered by an expression, used in evergreen top-N and ranking patterns.

nodes.name: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS
nodes.summary: DAX query function that returns a summary table, automatically eliminating rows where all measures are BLANK as an optimization.

nodes.name: DAX Studio
nodes.summary: Free external tool for DAX performance diagnostics that exposes storage engine and formula engine timings, server timings, and query plans.

nodes.name: Power BI Performance Analyzer
nodes.summary: Built-in Power BI Desktop tool that measures per-visual render time broken down into DAX query, visual display, and other overhead components.

edges.description: Local.ComputeForBestProds demonstrates the Local.* wrapper pattern by mapping model-specific columns to a model-independent top-N library function.
Local.ComputeForBestProds uses TOPN internally to enumerate top-N products per year.
The Local.* pattern formalizes the distinction between model-dependent wrappers and model-independent library functions.
The migration process produces Local.* wrappers as the model-specific layer in front of the refactored UDF library.
Migration categorizes parameters into NUMERIC and AnyRef types, which correspond to value vs expression parameter types that define model independence.
The DaxPatterns.LikeForLike.EntityStatus function exemplifies model-independent design by accepting date, entity, and table columns as parameters.
The PREVIOUS-based YoY% pattern is a visual calculation that operates on the virtual table structure using PREVIOUS() on the COLUMNS axis.
VC with PREVIOUS can be faster than measures for small virtual tables but is slower for large sparse tables due to densification overhead.
Performance Analyzer is the first-stop tool that identifies which visual is slow but cannot diagnose why.
DAX Studio is the diagnostic tool that exposes SE/FE timings and query plans to explain why a query is slow.
The warehouse analogy illustrates how Storage Engine performs fast parallel scans across column data.
The warehouse analogy illustrates how Formula Engine performs sequential operations on summarized results.
Per-level conditional formatting measures use SWITCH TRUE dispatch with REMOVEFILTERS or ALLSELECTED inside each branch to determine comparison totals.
SWITCH TRUE dispatch uses ISINSCOPE to detect the current hierarchy level for measure-based per-level logic.
SWITCH TRUE dispatch uses ISATLEVEL to detect the current hierarchy level for visual calculation-based per-level logic.
The level-dispatch pattern requires most-specific-first ordering so that leaf-level branches match before ancestor branches.
The specificity ordering principle is demonstrated with ISINSCOPE checks where ISINSCOPE(Date[Month]) must be tested before ISINSCOPE(Date[Year]).
